Both files are fixed. Here's a summary of every change:

---

### Root cause
The installed framework (`framework-arduinoespressif32 @ 3.20017` = Arduino-ESP32 **2.x**) uses the **old LEDC API**. The code was written for the newer **3.x** API where a single `ledcAttach(pin, freq, res)` call handles everything.

### What changed

**`include/MicromouseMotor.h`**
| Old (3.x API) | New (2.x API) |
|---|---|
| `MicromouseMotor(in1, in2)` | `MicromouseMotor(in1, in2, ch1Num, ch2Num)` — two LEDC channel numbers added |
| `ledcAttach(pinIN1, freq, res)` | `ledcSetup(ch1, freq, res)` + `ledcAttachPin(pinIN1, ch1)` |
| `ledcWrite(pinIN1, duty)` | `ledcWrite(ch1, duty)` — all writes now go through channel number |

**`src/main.cpp`**
- `leftMotor(MOTOR_L_IN1, MOTOR_L_IN2)` → `leftMotor(MOTOR_L_IN1, MOTOR_L_IN2, 0, 1)` — assigns LEDC channels 0 and 1 to the left motor

> **Note:** If you add a second motor later, give it channels 2 and 3 (e.g. `rightMotor(MOTOR_R_IN1, MOTOR_R_IN2, 2, 3)`). The ESP32-S3 has 8 low-speed + 8 high-speed LEDC channels available.

        "+        Serial.println(F(\"[IR] begin() — configuring emitter pins as OUTPUT, receiver pins as INPUT\"));",
        "+",

        "+        pinMode(EMIT_LF,  OUTPUT); digitalWrite(EMIT_LF,  LOW);",
        "+        pinMode(EMIT_L45, OUTPUT); digitalWrite(EMIT_L45, LOW);",
        "+        pinMode(EMIT_L,   OUTPUT); digitalWrite(EMIT_L,   LOW);",
        "+        pinMode(EMIT_R,   OUTPUT); digitalWrite(EMIT_R,   LOW);",
        "+        pinMode(EMIT_R45, OUTPUT); digitalWrite(EMIT_R45, LOW);",
        "+        pinMode(EMIT_RF,  OUTPUT); digitalWrite(EMIT_RF,  LOW);",

        "+        pinMode(RX_LF,  INPUT);",
        "+        pinMode(RX_L45, INPUT);",
        "+        pinMode(RX_L,   INPUT);",
        "+        pinMode(RX_R,   INPUT);",
        "+        pinMode(RX_R45, INPUT);",
        "+        pinMode(RX_RF,  INPUT);",
        "+",
        "+        // Zero readings",
        "+        for (int i = 0; i < IR_COUNT; i++) raw[i] = 0;",

        "+        Serial.println(F(\"[IR] update() done\"));",
        "+    }",
        "+",
        "+    // --------------------------------------------------------------------------",
        "+    // get() — return raw differential value for a given sensor",
        "+    // --------------------------------------------------------------------------",
        "+    int get(IRSensor s) const {",

        "+    // --------------------------------------------------------------------------",

        "+",

        "+                       raw[IR_RIGHT_SIDE],  wallRight()      ? \"YES\" : \"no\");",
        "+        Serial.printf( \"[IR]   Right-45    (R45) raw=%4d  wall=%s\\n\",",
        "+                       raw[IR_RIGHT_45],    wallDiagRight()  ? \"YES\" : \"no\");",
        "+        Serial.printf( \"[IR]   Right-Front (RF)  raw=%4d  wall=%s\\n\",",
        "+                       raw[IR_RIGHT_FRONT], wallFrontRight() ? \"YES\" : \"no\");",
        "+        Serial.printf( \"[IR]   Combined: FRONT=%s  LEFT=%s  RIGHT=%s\\n\",",
        "+                       wallFront() ? \"WALL\" : \"open\",",
        "+                       wallLeft()  ? \"WALL\" : \"open\",",
        "+                       wallRight() ? \"WALL\" : \"open\");",
        "+        Serial.println(F(\"[IR] =========================\"));",
        "+    }",
        "+};"

Everything is in place. Here's a complete summary of what was built:

---

## What was written — full overview

### New file: `include/MicromouseMaze.h` (306 lines)
The flood-fill solver. Everything is explained step-by-step in Serial output:

| Feature | Detail |
|---|---|
| **16×16 BFS flood-fill** | Full BFS from all goal cells outward; runs in <1 ms |
| **Wall encoding** | 4-bit per cell (N/E/S/W); `setWall()` automatically mirrors to the neighbour cell |
| **Goal cells** | Default: centre-4 for competition; `setGoalSingle()` for debugging |
| **`bestDirection()`** | Picks the neighbour with the lowest flood value — this is the navigation decision |
| **`printFlood()` / `printWalls()` / `printVisited()`** | Full 16×16 grid dumps to Serial |

### New file: `include/MicromouseIR.h` (170 lines)
Differential IR reading (ambient-subtracted), all 6 sensors, wall helpers:
- `update()` prints `ambient`, `lit`, `diff` for every sensor every call
- `wallFront()` / `wallLeft()` / `wallRight()` for maze logic
- `printStatus()` shows all 6 sensor values plus combined front/left/right result

### Updated headers — verbose logging added
| File | What's new |
|---|---|
| `MicromouseMotor.h` | `label` param ("LEFT"/"RIGHT"); every `drive()`, `brake()`, `coast()` logs direction, raw PWM |
| `MicromouseEncoder.h` | Thread-safe `getTicks()` (interrupt guard); `printStatus()`; constructor label |
| `MicromouseIMU.h` | I2C error check on wake; per-sample calibration prints; `printStatus()`; `update()` logs every integration step |

### Rewritten `src/main.cpp` (701 lines) — full robot FSM
```
IDLE → (button press) → CALIBRATE → EXPLORE → GOAL_REACHED → STOP
                                       ↑ loop until goal
```

| FSM State | What it does |
|---|---|
| **IDLE** | Waits for BUTTON_1, debounced |
| **CALIBRATE** | Re-calibrates IMU, resets encoders + maze |
| **EXPLORE** | Per-cell: sense IR → update walls → flood-fill → pick direction → turn → drive |
| **GOAL_REACHED** | Stops, beeps buzzer 3×, dumps full maze maps |
| **STOP** | Coast, print status every 5 s, button restarts |

Every function logs its inputs, outputs, and intermediate steps. Serial output is tagged with `[MODULE]` prefixes so you can grep specific systems during debugging.

### Key numbers to calibrate on your robot
| Constant | Location | Default | What to change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TRACK_WIDTH_MM` | `main.cpp` | 74.0 mm | Measure wheel-to-wheel contact distance |
| `IR_THRESH_FRONT/SIDE/DIAG` | `MicromouseIR.h` | 800/500/600 | Calibrate against real maze wall at cell-center |
| `Kp / Ki / Kd` | `main.cpp` | 1.5/0.8/0.05 | Tune PID on flat surface first |
| `CELL_MM` | `main.cpp` | 180.0 mm | Standard cell = 180 mm |
